summary: This note summarizes minimum legal ages for buying and consuming alcohol in several countries and regions, with the most common age being 18. It covers Mexico, where every state sets the minimum at 18, and North America, where limits range from 18 to 21. It also covers South America, where Guyana and Paraguay are exceptions. The passage is duplicated in the source, with the same text appearing twice.
one_line: Overview of minimum legal drinking and purchase ages in Mexico, North America and South America, mostly 18 with exceptions.
key_facts: The minimum age to buy and consume alcoholic beverages in Mexico is regulated by each state, but all states set a minimum age of 18 years.
In no Mexican state is it illegal for minors to buy and consume alcohol.
The most common minimum age to purchase and consume alcohol worldwide is 18 years, according to the note.
In North America, age limits vary between 18 and 21 years of age.
Throughout the United States the minimum legal age to purchase any alcoholic beverage from a shop, supermarket, liquor store, bar, club or other licensed premises is 21 years.
In Canada each province decides its own minimum age to buy or consume alcohol.
Most Canadian provinces have a minimum drinking age of 19 years.
Alberta, Manitoba and Quebec have set a minimum age of 18 years in Canada.
In South America all countries set a minimum purchase age of 18 years, except Guyana and Paraguay.
In Guyana, minors aged 16 or 17 may consume a glass of beer, wine or cider in a restaurant provided they buy a meal.
Paraguay is the only country with a minimum legal purchase and drinking age of 20 years.
The source text repeats the same paragraphs about age limits twice.
